violations.name: Missing Form I-9
violations.criminal: A pattern or practice of knowingly hiring unauthorized workers is a federal crime (8 U.S.C. §1324a(f)).
violations.note: 28 CFR §85.5, table 1, seen on eCFR November 14, 2026: an I-9 paperwork violation (8 U.S.C. 1324a(e)(5)) costs $288 to $2,861 per form for penalties assessed after July 3, 2025 (90 FR 29447). Knowingly employing a worker without authorization is $716 to $5,724 per worker on a first order. Every employer must complete Form I-9 for every person hired and keep it three years after hire or one year after employment ends, whichever is later. Game formula: four forms at the low end ($1,152), capped at four forms at the high end ($11,444).

violations.name: Tax returns not filed
violations.note: IRS failure-to-file page, seen November 14, 2026: 5% of the unpaid tax for each month or part of a month late, up to 25%; for a return more than 60 days late the minimum is $525 (returns due after December 31, 2025) or 100% of the tax, whichever is less. New York adds 10% of the sales tax due for the first month and 1% for each month after, up to 30%, minimum $50 (Tax Law §1145(a)(1)(i), seen). Game formula is my estimate for a shop that collects about $4,500 of sales tax a month: the $525 minimum plus $450 for every month without returns.

violations.name: No workers' compensation coverage
violations.criminal: A misdemeanor with a $1,000-$5,000 fine for an employer of five or fewer people; a class E felony with a $5,000-$50,000 fine for more than five (WCL §52(1)(a)).
violations.note: Workers' Compensation Board, seen November 14, 2026: up to $2,000 for each 10-day period without coverage (up to $6,000 a month), or no more than two times the cost of compensation for the payroll of that period; by the time the first penalty notice arrives it may exceed $12,000. On top: the unpaid premium (1.0 x saved). Failing to cover five or fewer employees within 12 months is a misdemeanor with a $1,000-$5,000 fine; more than five is a class E felony with $5,000-$50,000. A stop-work order under §141-a halts all business until coverage is in place. The 3 closure days are my estimate of how fast a policy can be bought.

taxes.name: Disability benefits insurance (employer part)
taxes.appliesIf: every employer with one or more employees
taxes.note: NYSIF disability benefits standard rates effective January 1, 2026 (seen): statutory premium $0.10 per $100 of payroll capped at $340 a week = $17.68 per person a year, minimum annual premium $60 (so a shop with three or fewer workers pays $60); the employer may withhold up to 0.5% of wages, at most $0.60 a week, from each worker. $17.68 / $40,320 = 0.04% of a full-time wage. Paid Family Leave is paid by the worker through payroll deduction: 0.432% of wages, at most $411.91 in 2026 (seen at paidfamilyleave.ny.gov).

taxes.name: Federal unemployment tax (FUTA)
taxes.appliesIf: every employer; 0.6% on the first $7,000 of each worker's wages
taxes.note: Seen at IRS Topic 759: 6.0% on the first $7,000 paid to each employee, less a credit of up to 5.4% for state unemployment tax = 0.6%, at most $42 per worker a year. Game rate is the effective share: $42 / $40,320 = 0.10% of payroll (with the D12 barista wage of $18: $42 / $34,560 = 0.12%). US DOL final 2026 credit reductions (updated November 12, 2026, seen): only California (1.5%) and the Virgin Islands; New York is not on the list, so 0.6% holds for 2026.

taxes.name: Workers' compensation insurance
taxes.appliesIf: most employers with one or more employees
taxes.note: Seen at the Workers' Compensation Board: coverage is mandatory for most employers of one or more employees, and deducting its cost from wages is a misdemeanor. The premium is quoted per $100 of payroll by job class and claims history, so there is no single rate: you need a quote. Game planning rate, my estimate: 2% of payroll. Anchors: Insureon reports coffee shops pay $88 a month ($1,059 a year) on average across the US (seen); New York's overall loss cost level fell 21.9% from October 1, 2026 (NYCIRB filing approved by DFS, seen through search). New York uses its own class codes (restaurants 9071-9074 per brokers); the restaurant loss cost per $100 was not found.

taxes.name: NY unemployment insurance (new employer)
taxes.appliesIf: every employer; 4.1% on the first $17,600 of each worker's wages
taxes.note: Seen at NY DOL: new employer rate 4.1% for 2026 (range 1.7%-9.5%) and a 2026 wage base of $17,600, so at most $721.60 per worker a year. The engine multiplies one rate by the whole payroll, so the game rate is the effective share for a full-time worker: $721.60 / $40,320 ($21 x 160 h x 12) = 1.79%; at the D12 cafe barista wage of $18 ($34,560 a year) it is 2.09%. The shared file serves every niche, so the rate is left at 1.79%; a per-worker cap in the engine would remove the guess. For a $17 x 140 h worker ($28,560 a year) the true share is 2.53%. Filed quarterly on Form NYS-45.

statutory.note: Seen November 14, 2026: Social Security 6.2% on wages up to $184,500 and Medicare 1.45% (IRS Publication 15, 2026); FUTA 6.0% on $7,000 less up to 5.4% credit (IRS Topic 759); NY UI new employer rate 4.1% and wage base $17,600 for 2026 (NY DOL); NYC minimum wage $17.00 in 2026 and still $17.00 on January 1, 2027 because one of the law's off-ramp conditions was met; tipped food service cash wage $11.35 + $5.65 credit for 2026 and 2027 (NY DOL); MCTMT threshold $312,500 a quarter (Form MTA-305 instructions); LLC $200 and Certificate of Publication $50 (NYS DOS); single-member LLC fee $25 (NYS Tax). CRT and UBT values were not reopened: nyc.gov refuses automated requests from this session.

shortcuts.name: Pay staff in cash, off the books
shortcuts.what: No payroll taxes, no workers' comp, no pay stubs: you keep about 11.6% of payroll each month. A tax audit or one unhappy worker brings back the taxes for both halves, plus penalties.
shortcuts.note: My arithmetic from rates seen: employer FICA 7.65% (IRS Pub. 15, 2026) + NY UI 1.79% effective (4.1% on the first $17,600, NY DOL) + FUTA 0.10% effective (IRS Topic 759) + workers' comp 2% planning rate + disability 0.04% (NYSIF 2026) = 11.58% of payroll.

shortcuts.name: Book employees as 1099 contractors
shortcuts.what: You skip employer payroll taxes and insurance, about 10% of payroll. People who work your schedule on your equipment are employees: the state bills the taxes back with interest.
shortcuts.note: My arithmetic: the same employer taxes without the workers' comp planning rate, 7.65% + 1.79% + 0.10% + 0.04% = 9.58%, rounded to 10%.

shortcuts.name: Ring cash sales off the register
shortcuts.what: About a tenth of sales never reaches the books: you keep the sales tax on it and pay no income tax on it, about 3% of sales in all. Auditors compare card sales, supplier invoices and supplies used.
shortcuts.note: My arithmetic: a tenth of sales off the books keeps 10% x 8.875% = 0.89% of sales in sales tax (NYC rate, Pub. 718) plus income and self-employment tax on the profit of those sales, 10% x 72% gross margin x 31.1% = 2.24%: about 3.1% of sales.

shortcuts.name: Spend the sales tax you collected
shortcuts.what: You file the return but hold back collected sales tax worth 4.5% of sales. It works like a loan from the state at 10% for the first month and 1% for each month after, and you are personally liable for it.
shortcuts.note: Game cap, see extra.shortcutNotes: 4.5% of sales, about half of the 8.875% a cafe collects (Pub. 718) and all of the 4.5% a barbershop collects. Late remittance: 10% for the first month and 1% a month after, up to 30% (Tax Law §1145, seen).

shortcuts.name: Skip workers' compensation insurance
shortcuts.what: Saves the premium, about 2% of payroll. The state can fine up to $2,000 for every 10 days without coverage and post a stop-work order; if someone is hurt, you pay the claim yourself.
shortcuts.note: The game's planning premium of 2% of payroll (taxes.workers_comp). Insureon reports coffee shops pay about $88 a month on average across the US (seen); a New York quote depends on class code and payroll.

shortcuts.name: Pay straight time for overtime
shortcuts.what: Hours over 40 a week are paid at the normal rate instead of time and a half, about 4% of payroll. A wage claim reaches back six years and doubles what you owe.
shortcuts.note: My arithmetic: if 8% of paid hours are over 40 a week, skipping the half-time premium saves 8% x 0.5 = 4% of payroll.

shortcuts.name: Unpaid opening and closing time
shortcuts.what: Staff set up before clocking in and clean after clocking out: about 8% of hours go unpaid, which pushes real pay below the legal wage. Owed back double, plus penalties.
shortcuts.note: My arithmetic: 15 minutes before and 20 minutes after an 8-hour shift = 35 / 480 = 7.3% of hours, rounded to 8%.

shortcuts.name: Run personal bills through the business
shortcuts.what: Groceries, the family phone plan and the car go on the business card as expenses, cutting taxable profit: worth about $450 a month in tax. An audit disallows them and adds 20%, or 75% for fraud.
shortcuts.note: My arithmetic: about $1,450 a month of personal spending booked as expenses x the game's 31.1% profit tax (17% income + 14.13% self-employment) = $450.

shortcuts.name: Hire without Form I-9
shortcuts.what: No ID check, no form, start tomorrow. Saves a little paperwork for each hire. A federal audit fines every missing form, whether or not the worker is allowed to work.
shortcuts.note: My estimate: about half an hour of the owner's time per hire at $30 an hour = $15. The fine is $288-$2,861 per form (28 CFR 85.5, seen).

shortcuts.name: Skip the bookkeeper and file nothing
shortcuts.what: No bookkeeper and no quarterly returns: saves about $400 a month. Late-filing penalties grow every month, and with no return the state estimates what you owe for you.
shortcuts.note: Equals the cafe pack's bookkeeping line ($400 a month, research notes estimate). The IRS minimum failure-to-file penalty is $525 for returns due after 2025 (seen).

shortcuts.name: Deny paid sick leave
shortcuts.what: Sick workers stay home unpaid or come in anyway: saves about $70 per worker a month. The city awards three times the unpaid wages or $250, whichever is more, plus $500 for each denial.
shortcuts.note: My arithmetic: 40 paid hours a year x $21 / 12 = $70 per worker a month (cafe pack after D12: 40 x $18 / 12 = $60). DCWP penalty: three times the unpaid wages or $250, plus $500 per denial (first pass; nyc.gov not reachable from this session).

shortcuts.name: Refuse cash
shortcuts.what: Card only: no cash counting, no bank runs, about $150 a month saved. Stores in New York City must accept cash: $750 for the first violation, $1,350 for the second, $1,500 after that.
shortcuts.note: My estimate: about $150 a month of counting, bank runs and change orders. Refusing cash costs $750, $1,350, then $1,500 per violation (NYC Business restaurant page, 6 RCNY §6-72, seen).
